reason: The winding drum needs a secure mounting before it can lift a load.
expectation: The drum and bracket will attach to the crane frame.

alternatives.reason: The crank may need to be assembled with the drum first.

effect: The drum and crank had to be assembled first; the hand winch is now ready to mount.
reaction: The explanation of the longer crank's trade-off is useful.
reason: The assembled winch needs a mounting on the crane to wind the lifting cord.
expectation: The hand winch will attach to the crane frame.

effect: The hand winch is mounted on the crane, ready for the lifting cord.
reason: The cord and hook can connect the winch to a load.
expectation: The cord will be routed from the winch over the pulley, with the hook ready to hold a load.

effect: The crane now has a lifting line; it still needs a way to hold a load safely.
reaction: The cord installation went as expected.
reason: The pawl should engage the ratchet to hold the drum while the release lever allows controlled lowering.
expectation: The holding and release mechanism will attach to the crane's winch.

alternatives.reason: The crane may need ballast before its holding mechanism is fitted.

effect: The pawl can hold the drum, but the crane still needs protection against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and stabilizing the crane is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help stabilize the crane before testing a load.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear of the crane and help resist tipping.

alternatives.reason: A light test might reveal how the crane behaves before adding ballast.

effect: The ballast cannot be combined yet, so I will test the rigged crane first.
reaction: I was surprised the ballast could not be fitted before testing.
reason: The padded weight offers a small test load for the rigged crane.
expectation: The crane will lift the test weight and reveal whether it needs stabilization.

effect: The test showed that the pawl holds the rope, but the crane needs better balance before lifting a load.
reaction: The test made the difference between holding and balancing clear.
reason: The rear ballast should counter the forward tipping seen in the test.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear and help keep the crane's feet down.

effect: The ballast keeps the feet down during the low test, and the pawl holds the drum; controlled lowering requires holding the crank while easing the release.
reaction: The test makes the separate jobs of ballast and pawl clear.
reason: The stabilized crane is ready to try lifting, holding and lowering the cargo basket.
expectation: The crane will lift the basket, hold it on the pawl and lower it gently.

effect: The basket test completed the goal: the crane lifted, held and gently lowered its load.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate safety measures work together in the final lift.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low test and ballast adjustment were most worthwhile because they showed why holding the rope is different from preventing the crane from tipping.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt to mount the drum was a minor detour; the drum first needed its crank assembled.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the ballast could not be fitted until the test had revealed the tipping problem.

arbitrary.text: Having to demonstrate tipping before fitting the already-available ballast felt somewhat arbitrary, even though the test explained its purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the crane's tests and explanations made the mechanisms understandable and worth exploring, despite the restricted assembly order.
